newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs dismiss woes, keep up good appearance.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs dismiss woes, keep up good appearance.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds tailed Bunds into higher regions on Thursday on the back of firmer U.S. Treasuries as traders wondered how long the market would ignore domestic setbacks.

They said that a first-time rating of Aa1 by Moody's for Belgian franc-denominated Treasury bonds, instead of the higher Aaa rating, and quarreling between government coalition partners over a bribery scandal, could potentially weigh on OLOs.
"But it's being completely ignored," said Dirk Laenen at CERA Bank. "We remain very strong and the (10-year yield) spread (with Bunds) doesn't budge."
The 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread was unchanged at plus five basis points. The benchmark 2007 OLO yielded 5.83 percent, down from 5.87 on Wednesday.

Only the franc has so far suffered from a crisis in one of the coalition parties related to a bribery scandal. Cracks have appeared in the coalition with a senior partner calling for the removal of controversial figures from the PS socialist party.

Since the scandal broke the franc has slipped towards its midpoint in the European exchange rate mechanism of 20.6255 to the mark. But traders said there was no talk of a government crisis and did not believe the midpoint would be breached.
Foreign interest in OLOs remained minimal, but Laenen said the market continued to see buying interest by domestic institutionals.
"Apparently Belgian portfolios still have to buy OLOs, it's their only alternative. They would get just three percent in the repo against up to around 4.5 percent in OLOs to five years.
"Those holding on to liquidity would miss out on 1.5 percent each day so people continue to invest in OLOs," he said.
He added that business was normal in all segments of the curve, which continued to remain very steep.
